missing_pages.title: Proof before 'done': make the agent show it works
missing_pages.what_it_teaches: A reader-followable routine for ask-for-proof. (1) Never accept 'all tests pass': ask for the command and its output, and audit each progress claim against a tool result. (2) Pick the check that fits the change: a quick live try (spike) for throwaway work, a test worth keeping, or running it like a user. (3) Red/green with agents: see the new test fail first, then pass. (4) Anti-gaming prompts: 'write a general solution, not one that only works for the test inputs', 'if a test looks wrong, tell me, do not change it'; how to spot a deleted, skipped or weakened test and a hard-coded return value in the diff. (5) When a defect gets through, add the test that would have caught it. (6) On a risky job, check each step's result before the next starts. Worked example with a real stuck-test transcript.
missing_pages.why_it_matters: This is the first level most members must reach and the single biggest hole: the playbook has the TDD loop and the Write-Test Cycle, but nothing says what proof to ask for, how to tell a fake green from a real one, or what to do when the agent edits the test. Today three challenges (special-casing tests, reward hacking beyond linter configs, laziness) have no how-to anywhere. An L1-L2 member who has been burned by 'it said done' has nowhere to go.
